bib.title: FRESHLLMS: REFRESHING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS WITH SEARCH ENGINE AUGMENTATION

question: How factual are LLMs on questions that need current or changing world knowledge or that carry false premises, and can search-engine results placed in the prompt fix it?
hypothesis: Plainly implied: grounding the prompt in up-to-date search results, in order and in number, raises factuality over parametric knowledge alone.
contributions: FRESHQA, a dynamic QA benchmark with never-, slow-, fast-changing and false-premise questions, to be updated regularly
Benchmark of closed and open LLMs with a two-mode (RELAXED/STRICT) human evaluation of more than 50K judgements
FRESHPROMPT, a few-shot in-context method that injects Google Search evidence, with sensitivity and ablation analyses

method.summary: 600 human-written questions (500 test, 100 dev, 15 demos) are answered by LLMs at temperature 0 with no retrieval, then by GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 with FRESHPROMPT (Google Search results formatted oldest to newest plus 5 few-shot demonstrations with reasoning). Authors judge each response under RELAXED (primary answer correct) and STRICT (no hallucination or outdated claim); all models were run on 26 April 2023.
method.task: open-domain question answering on time-sensitive and false-premise questions; search-augmented prompting

datasets.name: FRESHQA
datasets.size: 600 questions: test 500 (125 per type), dev 100 (25 per type), 15 demonstration examples; remainder discarded
datasets.split: test set used; dev reserved for future work and not used in this paper
datasets.source: NLP researchers and Upwork freelancers ($2 per example); released at github.com/freshllms/freshqa
datasets.preprocessing: manual review for well-formedness, duplicate and invalid removal, answer and URL verification, supplementary valid answers added; questions whose answers change more often than weekly excluded; next review date recorded

datasets.name: TriviaQA 5-shot demonstrations (as used in Sun et al. 2023)
datasets.preprocessing: used as few-shot and CoT prompt for the baseline models

models.name: Google Search (answer box or top-1 snippet)
Perplexity.ai (concise answers)
models.architecture: GPT-3.5 plus Bing Search at evaluation time

other.note: authors' few-shot prompt reused; only the final answer is evaluated
which LLM is the judge is not stated in the text

inference.decoding: greedy: most likely token at each step
inference.samples: one response per question; one run on 26 April 2023; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: baselines: non-chat models get 'Q: <question>\nA: '; few-shot and CoT use the 5-shot TriviaQA demonstrations. FRESHPROMPT: question, then retrieved evidences sorted oldest to newest, then reasoning and answer; m=5 demonstrations at the start; ChatGPT and GPT-4 are given the current date.
inference.retrieval: Google Search via SerpApi, query = question verbatim, one query per question; evidences: o organic results, r related questions, a crowdsourced QA items, plus answer box and knowledge graph snippets; keep top n by date (closest to end of prompt)

parameters.premise check text: Please check if the question contains a valid premise before answering

other.note: the OpenAI API is non-deterministic even at temperature 0; PPLX.AI decoding not controllable

metrics.name: RELAXED accuracy
metrics.definition: response credited if the primary answer is correct; ill-formed, hallucinated or outdated extra information that does not impact the primary answer is allowed; false-premise questions need an explicit rebuttal

metrics.name: STRICT accuracy
metrics.definition: as RELAXED, but any hallucination, however minor, gets no credit; 'knowledge cutoff' hedges accepted only if the knowledge is evidently unchanged

metrics.name: STRICT-RELAXED gap
metrics.definition: difference between the two modes, read as a measure of hallucination

metrics.name: Agreement with human raters
metrics.definition: exact accuracy between two raters or between FreshEval and a rater on 100 sampled answers (50 valid-premise, 50 false-premise) per mode

baselines: T5, PaLM, Flan, Codex, ChatGPT without retrieval
eval.protocol: Authors judged every response by hand (more than 50K judgements); two authors double-rated 100 answers per mode. Accuracy broken down by fast, slow, never, false-premise, before 2022 vs since 2022, one-hop vs multi-hop. No significance tests or seeds.

prompts.text: Please evaluate the response to each given question under a relaxed evaluation, where hallucinations, outdated information, and ill-formed answers are allowed, as long as the primary answer is accurate. Please credit the response only if it provides a confident and definitive answer, or the correct answer can be obviously inferred from the response. The primary or final answer when standing alone must be accurate. Any additional information that is provided must not contradict the primary answer or reshape one's perception of it. For false-premise questions, the response must point out the presence of a false premise to receive credit.

limits: Answers need regular manual updating; between updates some answers go stale.
FRESHPROMPT relies on Google Search; behaviour with search engines lacking answer boxes is unknown.
Only one search query per question, no decomposition.
Questions are simple English; multilingual and long-form QA untested.
In-context learning may underperform fine-tuning on new knowledge.
Judging was by the authors only; single run at temperature 0 on one date; no confidence intervals; test set 500 questions (125 per type).
Models served by APIs change over time and are non-deterministic; Perplexity.ai decoding not controlled.
Lazaridou et al. 2022 not compared because of its 50-call inference cost.
Results date from April 2023 model versions; GPT-4 and ChatGPT now browse the web (footnote 7).

terms.definition: never-changing: the answer almost never changes; slow-changing: typically changes over several years; fast-changing: typically changes within a year or less; false-premise: questions whose premises are factually incorrect and must be rebutted
RELAXED measures only whether the main answer is correct; STRICT measures whether all claims are factual and up-to-date (no hallucination)
an automatic metric that uses few-shot in-context learning to teach an LLM to judge model responses
